newsitem.title: UK: INSIGHT - Weak copper could test $2,000 level.
newsitem.headline: INSIGHT - Weak copper could test $2,000 level.

text.p: 3 MONTH CLOSE * SUPPORT * RESIST * RSI14 * MA10 * MA30
After a second bearish close this week on Wednesday, copper could be heading for a test of the $2,200-$2,210 level, analysts said on Thursday.
A move below that was not ruled out but the oversold ratio was rising suggesting support from short-covering was possible.
COPPER -
A $72 trading range on Wednesday did not fully reflect early weakness or copper's close below Tuesday's low which set up bearish portends for Thursday.

Behind the technical picture estimates of the amount of Chinese copper moving to London Metal Exchange (LME) warehouse range between 30,000 and 80,000 tonnes which has put the market on the backfoot as the summer shutdown season begins in the northern hemisphere.
Thursday's initial target was $2,210 but $2,200 and down to $2,185 were possible if trendline support at the first point broke, analysts said.
Yesterday's bounce was reasonably predictable given the market was oversold but whether or not the bounce level of $2,245 survives a slide again is less certain.
Conversely a correction could catch the bears out.
"Look for initial downside tests but with the metal looking increasingly oversold (21.8) we remain wary of a corrective bounce," said broker Rudolf Wolff and Co's technical analyst Martin Squires.
At 0725 GMT copper was indicated at $2,255/$2,260 up $17 from Wednesday's late trading level.
ALUMINIUM -
The short covering bounce at $1,550 on Wednesday owed something to copper gaining support but it also reflected the bears' failure to trigger sell stops under the market, analysts said.
A continuation of the move was possible today after last night's close on the highs.
Amalgamated Metal trading's technical analyst Harry Creates forecast this implied "a test of fanline resistance at $1,574. A close above that would ease downward pressure," he said.
However other forecasters said rumoured builds in LME warehouse stocks suggested the upside will be capped for the medium term.
At 0735 GMT aluminium was indicted at $1,567/$1,569 about $6.00 above Wednesday's late trading level.
